question.text: Which behavioral bias involves overestimating one's ability to beat the market through stock picking?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XVII (p.91), optimism/confidence bias is the belief in one's ability to outperform based on prior investing successes; this can lead to unsuitable investment choices. The Trap: Herd mentality is following others; recency bias is extrapolating recent trends; loss aversion is the fear of losses. Optimism/confidence bias is specifically about overestimating personal skill. Note: Counter this bias with a written investment policy, systematic processes, and adherence to long-term retirement goals rather than ad-hoc stock picks.
